raw_case_text: We present the case of an 18-month-old female patient with PB following pneumonia. At 2 months of age, the patient was hospitalized due to pneumonia. At 6 months of age, she underwent a palliative bidirectional Glenn procedure (Fontan-type) due to CHD (double-inlet and double-outlet ventricle with common atrioventricular canal). The perioperative period was uneventful. Echocardiography at 12 and 18 months of age showed proper heart function (ejection fraction, 67%). At 18 months of age, she was again hospitalized due to pneumonia that remained unresolved after three courses of antibiotics in the home setting. Infiltration and atelectasis of the left upper lobe had been clinically suspected (because of dullness and diminished breath sounds over that region) and was confirmed by a chest X-ray. Blood pressure was normal. However, SpO2 was approximately 50% (having previously been at 70-80%). In addition, hypogammaglobulinemia was detected. In the differential diagnosis, we excluded atopy, cystic fibrosis, immunodeficiency disorders, viral infections (with cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, and pneumotropic viruses), and fungal infections (Aspergillus sp. and Candida sp.). Within a few days, her coughs were more productive and there was expectoration of small mucoid casts. Despite antibiotic treatment, gamma-globulin replacement therapy, oxygen therapy, and intensive chest physiotherapy, as well as the use of nebulized bronchodilators and mucolytics, there was no clinical improvement. On post-admission day 17, fiberoptic bronchoscopy (FB) revealed complete obliteration of the left bronchus. Application of suction allowed to remove bronchial casts, followed by bronchial lavage of that region (Figure 1). Cultures of the bronchial lavage fluid were negative for fungi and bacteria. Microscopic analysis of the material collected revealed type-1 bronchial casts. After the bronchoscopy, the inflammation of the left lobes was resolved. Treatment with azithromycin, systemic and inhaled steroids, () and enalapril maleate was initiated, as was the use of nebulized 3% NaCl solution plus a bronchodilator. One week after treatment initiation, a control FB revealed only small fragments of casts, which were removed easily and completely. On post-admission day 33, the patient was discharged.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 18-month-old girl with a history of bidirectional Glenn palliation for complex congenital heart disease presented with persistent pneumonia unresponsive to three outpatient antibiotic courses, worsening cyanosis, and productive cough with expectoration of mucoid bronchial casts.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Having undergone an uneventful palliative bidirectional Glenn procedure at 6 months of age for double-inlet/double-outlet ventricle with common atrioventricular canal, the patient was hospitalized at 18 months of age for left upper lobe pneumonia and atelectasis that failed three home antibiotic courses, accompanied by a drop in oxygen saturation from her 70-80% baseline to ~50% and subsequent expectoration of small mucoid bronchial casts.
subjective.past_medical_history: Complex congenital heart disease (double-inlet and double-outlet ventricle with common atrioventricular canal) status post palliative bidirectional Glenn procedure at 6 months of age (LVEF 67% on 12- and 18-month echocardiograms); prior hospitalization for pneumonia at 2 months of age.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for persistent productive cough, expectoration of small mucoid casts, and worsening hypoxemia/cyanosis.

objective.physical_examination: Normal blood pressure, severe hypoxemia with SpO2 ~50% (baseline 70-80%), and dullness to percussion with diminished breath sounds over the left upper lung lobe.
objective.routine_investigations: Chest X-ray confirmed left upper lobe infiltration and atelectasis. Echocardiography showed preserved ventricular function (EF 67%). Hypogammaglobulinemia was detected; diagnostic workup excluded atopy, cystic fibrosis, primary immunodeficiency disorders, viral infections (cytomegalovirus [CMV], Epstein-Barr virus [EBV], and pneumotropic viruses), and fungal infections (Aspergillus spp. and Candida spp.).
objective.advanced_workup: On hospital day 17, fiberoptic bronchoscopy (FB) revealed complete obliteration of the left mainstem bronchus by extensive branching mucoid casts; suction extraction and bronchial lavage removed the casts, with negative bacterial and fungal lavage cultures and microscopic histopathology confirming acellular/inflammatory type-1 plastic bronchitis casts (repeat FB 1 week later removed only small residual cast fragments).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis of type-1 plastic bronchitis (PB) following pneumonia in a child with bidirectional Glenn circulation, confirmed by bronchoscopic extraction and microscopic identification of type-1 bronchial casts (with CMV, EBV, pneumotropic viruses, Aspergillus, Candida, cystic fibrosis, and atopy ruled out). Following failure of initial antibiotics, IVIG replacement, oxygen, chest physiotherapy, and nebulized bronchodilators/mucolytics, bronchoscopic cast removal on day 17 (and repeat clearance 1 week later) combined with azithromycin, systemic and inhaled corticosteroids, sildenafil, enalapril maleate, and nebulized 3% hypertonic saline plus bronchodilators resolved the left lung atelectasis/inflammation, and the patient was discharged on hospital day 33.
